text:
sasha: Heads up — onboarding sample 'next-worker' started failing after I published v1.3.0. Cloudflare build errors out with \"No matching export for './'\" and wrangler dev just crashes.
ben: repro steps?
sasha: Clone + npm i + wrangler dev. Error log:
```
Error: Cannot find module './'
 at Module._resolveFilename (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:...) 
 at Function.resolve (internal/modules/cjs/helpers.js:...)
wrangler: failed to build
```
sasha: Our package.json exports currently look like:
```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
maya: I think the edge/worker resolver needs a specific conditional or a browser/worker mapping. Also TypeScript in some bundlers looks for types in exports or falls back weirdly.
priya: FWIW I saw auth/retry weirdness tied to ESM/CJS split: our CJS entry pulls node-fetch and our retry wrapper expects node-fetch Response. In the ESM/worker path it uses global fetch and the shapes differ (missing some props our wrapper checks), so retries skip or throw.
dan: Quick fix idea: expose explicit worker/import/type entrypoints in exports so wrangler and bundlers pick the right file. e.g.
```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "worker": "./dist/index.worker.mjs",
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs",
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
  }
}
```
june: I agree with adding a worker conditional + types. We should cut a patch (v1.3.1) and include a tiny smoke that runs wrangler build in CI to catch regressions.
ci-bot: ci/canary — check 12 failed, 1 failed because of samples/next-worker wrangler build error (exit code 1)
ben: I'll open a PR that adds the worker conditional and types export + a GH Action job that runs `wrangler build` against the sample. If it passes we can publish 1.3.1.
sasha: Thanks — @ben please also add a tiny integration test that simulates global fetch vs node-fetch shape so we catch retry mismatches.
ben: Will do. If tests fail we'll revert 1.3.0 and republish.
sasha: Cool. Tagging the release and eng-ml so they know SDK parity is flaky across exports. :pray:
